text:
Alex R: quick sync — planning to enable two runtime toggles for a small canary today: speculative_decoding=on and kv_cache_compaction=aggressive. Targeting 5% prod traffic in us-east (plus 100% internal). Rolling window 60m. Main goals: shave tail latency and reduce KV mem pressure during spikes. Will monitor quality regressions closely. :eyes:

Priya S: what are the regressions we're most worried about? hallucination risk with speculative? token-level drift?

Alex R: good q. speculative_decoding may change token probabilities slightly for early tokens — we'll watch top-1/top-3 divergence and bot-quality evals. KV compaction can change cache hit patterns; watch p99 generation time and memory delta. Set guardrails below.

Micha L: is this compatible with quantized kernels (4-bit) and our custom fused-attn kernels? any fallbacks?

Alex R: yes — runtime picks fallback paths. If kernel mismatch detected we auto-fallback to safe path (speculative disabled for that request). We added a kernel compatibility whitelist. For quantized models we keep spec on but use conservative beam budgets.

Jamie T: SRE checklist: expected mem increase? OOM risk? circuit-breaker thresholds?

Alex R: expecting <=10% mem change in steady state; peak could be higher for large batch loads. Circuit-breaker triggers we set: error_rate >= 0.5% over 5m OR p99 latency up 25% OR mem increase > 12% -> immediate rollback. Also will open a transient extra alert channel.

Priya S: can you paste the feature flag config you'll push so we can review?

Alex R: sure — here's the flag payload I'll push via ffctl.

```yaml
feature: runtime.optimizations.speculative_and_kv
owner: alexr
version: v1.3
toggles:
  speculative_decoding: true
  kv_cache_compaction: aggressive
canary:
  pct: 5
  audience: production
  regions: [us-east-1]
  duration_minutes: 60
metrics_to_monitor:
  - p99_latency_ms
  - error_rate_pct
  - mem_delta_pct
  - top1_divergence_pct
rollbacks:
  max_error_rate_pct: 0.5
  max_p99_latency_increase_ms: 25
  max_mem_increase_pct: 12
allowed_models: ["redwood-v2*", "openllm-*", "open*-quant4*"]
```

Micha L: fine with the allowed_models, but add explicit kernel_tags: ["fused-attn-v2", "matmul-fast"] to avoid weird kernel combos.

Alex R: good call. will add kernel_tags.

Jamie T: add a temporary SLO relax window? if p99 spikes briefly we shouldn't be paged unless sustained. Maybe suppress paging for 10m if auto-rollback will run?

Alex R: agreed. we'll set alerting: notify #eng-oncall for sustained violation >10m; otherwise post to #eng-runtime-incidents channel.

rollout-bot: Feature flag update queued: runtime.optimizations.speculative_and_kv by @alexr. Planned canary 5% in us-east-1, duration 60m. Audit id: rollout/2026/04/23/abc123.

Alex R: deploying now with the following ffctl command:

`ffctl set runtime.optimizations.speculative_and_kv --speculative=true --kv_compaction=aggressive --canary=5 --region=us-east-1 --owner=alexr --kernel_tags=fused-attn-v2,matmul-fast`

ops-bot: CI: canary config validated, no schema errors. Canary plan applied to service group `runtime-gpu-pool-us-east`.

Priya S: I'll queue a small prompt-suite run (20 prompts) against canary and control to track immediate divergence.

Micha L: i'll watch kernel telemetry and detour logs. if we see >10% compaction-induced cache churn i'll flip compaction to conservative.

Alex R: plan B if we get noisy results: rollback compaction only and keep speculative on for a follow-up 2% canary. If regressed quality then full rollback.

Jamie T: good. heads-up: I'll be on-call for the window. ping me in thread if anything looks off.

Alex R: thanks all — will post interim metrics at +15m and +45m.

(45m later)

Alex R: quick update — +15m: p99 latency -5ms overall, mem_delta +3%, error_rate unchanged, top1_divergence 0.2% on our quick-suite. so far so good. :tada:

Priya S: nice! continuing the longer eval now.

Micha L: kernel telemetry stable. no fallback triggers.

rollout-bot: Canary progress: runtime.optimizations.speculative_and_kv at 5% for 46m. No rollback conditions met. Audit id: rollout/2026/04/23/abc123.

Alex R: I'll promote to 20% tomorrow morning (internal notice to expand to eu-west as separate canary) unless objections.

Jamie T: approve, but do EU in a separate small canary; watch regional memory/disk pressure.

Priya S: ack. i'll run full 200-prompt eval on 20% canary when you promote.

Alex R: thanks everyone — closing thread for now, will reopen if anything changes.
